note: Each row is a public record as it was filed or published; the list shows everything the figures in this case were counted from. Being listed is not an accusation: the case file says what is established and what is not.

tables.title: San Francisco food aid each fiscal year: issued, paid in error, investigated, fraud found, disqualified
tables.what: One state fiscal year (July to June) of CalFresh food aid in San Francisco, as the county reported it to the State and the State published it.

columns.t: Federal year of that rate (September figure)
Estimated paid in error (rate times issued)
Fraud identified as a share of food aid issued

sources.t: CalFresh participation and benefit issuance by county and month (latest workbook; earlier years in the same series)
CalFresh Data Dashboard workbook: quality-control active error rate by county
DSS 466 Fraud Investigation Activity Report, by county and quarter (latest workbook; earlier years in the same series)

tables.how: Households and food aid issued: the State’s monthly issuance report (DFA 256, later CF 256) for San Francisco, households averaged and benefits added over the twelve months of each state fiscal year (the second list gives every month). Error rate: the State’s CalFresh dashboard figure for San Francisco in September, the full federal year that ends three months into the state fiscal year (federal 2025 for fiscal 2026); there is no September figure for federal 2020 and 2021, so fiscal 2021 has no rate. Investigations and fraud: the county’s DSS 466 reports, four quarters added up: items 1 to 3 and 6 to 8 (concluded), 1 and 6 (evidence found), 11 (dollars of fraud identified), 16, 17, 20, 21 (disqualified at a hearing or by waiver) and 24, 25, 28, 29 (disqualified through a prosecution or a consent agreement). The State hides any count from 1 to 10; each hidden disqualification cell is counted as 1 at the low end and 10 at the high end. The rule is scripts/analysis/benefits.py, run as it stands.
tables.limits: The error rate counts money paid too high and too low, mostly mistakes by the agency or the household, not deceit; it comes from a sample of cases and moves several points a year, so the dollar figure is an order of magnitude, not an audited loss. The State publishes the split between overpayment and underpayment for California only (fourth list). A low count of fraud found can mean little fraud or little looking; these reports cannot tell the two apart. Disqualifications may also be avoided by repayment agreements, which these reports do not count. Every row is a county total; nothing about any household is in these files.

tables.title: Every line of San Francisco’s quarterly fraud-investigation reports to the State, fiscal 2019 to 2026
tables.what: One line of one quarter’s DSS 466 Fraud Investigation Activity Report filed by San Francisco County, for food aid or cash aid, as the State published it.

columns.t: Quarter as the State labels it

sources.t: DSS 466 Fraud Investigation Activity Report, by county and quarter (latest workbook; earlier years in the same series)

tables.how: Every DSS 466 line for San Francisco County in the State’s extract for the quarters of state fiscal years 2019 to 2026 (1,632 lines). The "counted as" column shows which lines the case adds up: for fiscal 2026 the food-aid lines marked "evidence found" add up to 598, the "fraud dollars" lines to $466,321, and evidence found, no evidence and referred together to 1,370 concluded investigations.
tables.limits: Values are the county’s own counts as the State printed them. A blank value with "Hidden" is a count from 1 to 10 that the State does not print. A line counts investigations or people, not households, and says nothing about anyone in particular.

tables.title: Food aid issued in San Francisco, month by month, fiscal 2019 to 2026
tables.what: One month of the State’s CalFresh participation and issuance report for San Francisco County.

sources.t: CalFresh participation and benefit issuance by county and month (latest workbook; earlier years in the same series)

tables.how: Every month from July 2018 to June 2026 for San Francisco in the State’s issuance reports (96 months). The yearly figures in the first list are these months added up (benefits) or averaged (households).
tables.limits: Counts of households and people on the program, not of any one of them. The State changed the form in May 2024 (DFA 256 to CF 256); the totals carry across. Replacement benefits for stolen cards are reported separately and are not in these totals.

tables.title: The food-aid error rate the State publishes for San Francisco and for California, month by month
tables.what: One month’s quality-control "active error rate" in the State’s CalFresh dashboard, for San Francisco County or for California as a whole.

columns.t: Active error rate (share of dollars paid in the wrong amount)

sources.t: CalFresh Data Dashboard workbook: quality-control active error rate by county

tables.how: Every monthly figure in the dashboard workbook for San Francisco and for the State. The figure runs cumulatively through each federal year (October to September), so the September figure is the full-year rate; the case uses San Francisco’s September 2025 figure (12%) for fiscal 2026 and September 2018 (8%) for fiscal 2019.
tables.limits: A quality-control error rate is built from a sample of cases re-checked by State and federal reviewers. It counts overpayments and underpayments together and does not measure fraud. County rates come from small samples and move several points from year to year.

tables.how: The federal tables of payment error rates by state, read for California for every year in the download. The case quotes federal 2025: overpayments 10.06 points of a 10.93% error rate.
tables.limits: The federal government publishes the split for each state, not for each county, so how much of San Francisco’s error was money paid too high is not known. Federal 2020 and 2021 have no published rates (the pandemic waiver years).

tables.title: Every county: food-aid fraud investigations for each 10,000 households, fiscal 2026
tables.what: One California county’s DSS 466 food-aid investigation counts for state fiscal year 2026, set against its average number of food-aid households.

sources.t: DSS 466 Fraud Investigation Activity Report, by county and quarter (latest workbook; earlier years in the same series)
CalFresh participation and benefit issuance by county and month (latest workbook; earlier years in the same series)

tables.how: Every county with four published quarters in fiscal 2026 and ten or more months of households, plus the State total. Concluded investigations are items 1 to 3 and 6 to 8; households are the monthly average from the issuance report. The rank is among the 26 counties with 20,000 or more households, highest first; San Francisco is 15.
tables.limits: Counties staff and count investigations differently, so a ranking is a prompt for questions, not a verdict on which county is right. Hidden counts (1 to 10) are carried as ranges for disqualifications.

tables.title: Cases sent to San Francisco’s investigators from computer matches, each fiscal year
tables.what: One state fiscal year of the county’s DPA 482 income and eligibility verification reports (food aid and cash aid together), four quarters added up.

columns.t: Referred to investigators or the District Attorney
Overpayments found caused by the household (dollars)
Overpayments found caused by the agency (dollars)
Household-caused errors pending at the end of the second quarter

sources.t: DPA 482 Income and Eligibility Verification System report, by county and quarter (latest workbook)

tables.how: The DPA 482 lines for San Francisco for food aid and cash aid together, added over the four quarters of each state fiscal year that the State published in full. The agency-error columns of the newer workbooks are printed the other way round; the larger figure is taken as dollars, as the analysis does.
tables.limits: A referral is a computer match worth investigating, not a finding. The report covers food aid and cash aid together.

tables.title: Every arrest booked on a welfare-fraud code since 2014, and what the District Attorney did
tables.what: One arrest presented to the District Attorney in which a booked charge is a welfare-fraud section of the Welfare and Institutions Code (10980, 11483, 14107 or 14014). The person arrested is not named.

sources.t: District Attorney Actions Taken on Arrests Presented

tables.how: Every row of the District Attorney’s public file of actions taken on arrests whose booked charges include one of the four welfare-fraud sections, with an arrest date from 2014 on: the rule in scripts/analysis/benefits.py. 36 arrests; by year: 2014: 5, 2015: 1, 2016: 2, 2017: 2, 2018: 5, 2019: 4, 2021: 1, 2022: 2, 2023: 4, 2025: 10.
tables.limits: The person arrested is in this record as a benefit recipient and is never named; the incident and court numbers and the exact day are left out for the same reason. The file covers arrests presented to the District Attorney, not cases the county settled by repayment or an administrative hearing, and the charges booked can cover any welfare program, not only food aid.
